recognition: Recognized from the supplied documentation as UCI Student Performance (UCI 320), including Portuguese-language records and the cited Cortez and Silva 2008 introduction. This is input-based recognition; I am not relying on a remembered external result.
summary: I1 is a concrete, potentially useful support-allocation question beyond final-grade prediction. The supplied 649 records from two Portuguese schools include period grades, absences, travel-time categories, and existing support indicators, but no dated attendance, randomized support assignment, or reliable support timing. They can scope recruitment feasibility only. I sharpened the proposed trial estimand and downgraded the attendance mechanism claim: randomization can identify the equal-contact package contrast, while attendance remains a proximal outcome rather than an identified mediator.

candidates.title: Separate attendance-access support from tutoring at the first-period decision point
candidates.question: Among Portuguese-course students below a school-predeclared G1 threshold at the end of period 1, does an equal-scheduled-contact attendance-access and missed-lesson recovery offer improve period-2 G2 more than subject tutoring, and is that package contrast larger in a predeclared high-absence stratum?
candidates.new_claim: Support allocation may improve when the added-support package is matched to an attendance-access bottleneck rather than assuming all low G1 reflects subject-mastery difficulty. This is a proposal-only, falsifiable hypothesis, not a result in the supplied records.
candidates.input_delta: The input contains G1/G2, a total absence count, coarse travel-time categories, and support indicators, but not dated lesson attendance, instructional exposure, support assignment, intervention fidelity, or a randomized comparison. The proposed increment is an equal-contact randomized package contrast with an explicit baseline-absence interaction.
candidates.domain_value: If the package contrast is meaningfully larger for students with high baseline absence, schools could allocate added support by an actionable risk stratum; if not, a common tutoring route may be preferable. No support required as standard practice would be withheld.
known_basis_refs: official_documentation.additional_info: G1/G2 are first/second-period grades and G3 is final grade; G1 and G2 correlate with G3
official_documentation.variables: absences, traveltime, schoolsup, G1, G2
case.workflow: support understanding or allocation beyond final-grade prediction
case.unit: two Portuguese schools; support not randomized; limited survey timing metadata
data_profile: 649 rows; absences quartiles 0, 2, 6 and maximum 32; G1 and G2 each range 0-19
assumptions: The school defines an academically meaningful G1 eligibility threshold and high-absence rule before enrollment; exploratory thresholds in the requested calculation are not asserted as school policy.
Both added-support offers can have equal scheduled contact minutes, be delivered consistently, and supplement rather than replace standard or required support.
Randomization is feasible within school and baseline-risk strata, and the number of classrooms and students supports classroom-aware inference.
G2 is scored comparably across arms and aligned with material taught during the intervention period.
candidates.variables_and_units: Eligibility: G1 below a predeclared threshold (grade points, 0-20). Moderator: period-1 scheduled Portuguese lessons missed (count), grouped by a predeclared rule. Assigned offer: access-and-catch-up package versus subject tutoring (categorical), with equal scheduled contact minutes per student. Proximal outcome: period-2 attended scheduled Portuguese lessons (count and proportion); primary outcome: G2 grade points (0-20). Unit: student; account for classroom/teacher clustering.
candidates.testable_prediction: Frozen before tool returns: the intention-to-treat G2 contrast (access-and-catch-up minus tutoring, estimated with baseline G1 adjustment) will be positive and larger in the predeclared high-absence stratum than in the low-absence stratum. The access package is also predicted to increase period-2 attendance more than tutoring among high-absence students. An attendance increase without a meaningful G2 advantage does not support the academic-support claim.
candidates.alternative: Subject-mastery difficulty or general contact/attention is the main bottleneck, so tutoring matches or exceeds access-and-catch-up on G2 and the package contrast does not increase with baseline absence. Any attendance difference may fail to translate into learning.
candidates.discriminating_test: Preregister an individually randomized, equal-scheduled-contact comparison among eligible students at period-1 end, stratified by school and predeclared absence group. Keep normal support available in both arms. Record baseline G1 and dated scheduled/attended lessons, assigned offer, actual package components and contact minutes, G2, and class/teacher. Estimate intention-to-treat G2 by ANCOVA adjusting for G1, the treatment-by-absence interaction, and the corresponding attendance contrasts with classroom-aware uncertainty. Set the minimum meaningful G2 difference, missing-data rule, and analysis before enrollment. Treat attendance as a proximal outcome; a causal mediation claim would require additional assumptions and is not identified by this comparison alone.
candidates.feasible_with_current_data: Only an exploratory count and descriptive G2-G1 summary by provisional G1, absence, and travel-time strata can be computed to inform recruitment. Current records cannot identify the causal support contrast, attendance response, mediation, or prospective outcomes because assignment, timing, and dated attendance are absent.
candidates.required_new_data: Prospective eligibility and baseline G1; predeclared school threshold and absence rule; dated scheduled and attended Portuguese lessons in both periods; randomized offer and stratum; intervention components, fidelity, and delivered minutes; G2; class/teacher identifiers; and a preregistered minimum meaningful difference and analysis plan.
candidates.failure_condition: With adequate precision, reject the frozen routing prediction if the high-absence stratum shows no meaningful G2 advantage for access-and-catch-up over equal-contact tutoring, or if the predicted attendance advantage is absent. If attendance improves but G2 does not, reject the stronger claim that access recovery is the more useful academic support.
candidates.nearest_prior_query: Search for secondary-school randomized or quasi-randomized comparisons of attendance/access or missed-instruction recovery support against equal-contact subject tutoring, with baseline-absence moderation, dated attendance, and course-grade outcomes.

task.deliverable: A sharpened I1 proposal, one exploratory current-data feasibility request, and one focused prior-work query. No scientific computation or search has been run in this executor turn.
acceptance: Separate the randomized package effect from the observational descriptive evidence and avoid claiming identified mediation.
Specify G2 with baseline G1 adjustment as primary outcome, the predeclared absence interaction, equal scheduled contact, and an alternative that can defeat the prediction.
Retain standard support, measure dated attendance and intervention fidelity, and account for classroom/teacher clustering.

Use any computation only for recruitment and descriptive feasibility, not causal or prospective claims; use literature results only as returned and distinguish title-level coverage from verified findings.
task.proposed_computation: Count records below a provisional G1<10 threshold by absences>=6 versus <6 and traveltime category; summarize G2-G1 with uncertainty intervals only as an exploratory descriptive feasibility check. The supplied profile places G1's first quartile at 10 and absences' third quartile at 6, so these cut points are transparent data-anchored probes, not validated eligibility rules or school standards. Sparse cells would motivate dropping travel-time stratification or enlarging prospective recruitment.
task.proposed_search: Crossref search for secondary-school randomized or quasi-randomized attendance/access or missed-instruction recovery interventions compared with equal-contact subject tutoring, focusing on baseline-absence moderation, measured attendance, and period-grade outcomes. A close match would narrow the novelty claim to the exact population, package, or allocation interaction; titles alone do not establish results.

critique: The original wording treats attendance as a mediator, but package randomization alone does not identify an indirect effect through attendance; unmeasured post-randomization causes can confound attendance-G2 relations. Keep attendance as a proximal outcome unless a mediation design and assumptions are supplied.

A high-absence subgroup is not operationally fixed in the leader proposal, and long travel time was asked about without a distinct frozen interaction prediction. Predeclare one absence rule for the primary moderator; collect actual travel barriers as descriptive/context measures unless separately powered and preregistered.

Using raw G2-G1 change as the main comparison is vulnerable to baseline dependence and regression to the mean. Use randomized intention-to-treat G2 with baseline G1 adjustment as primary; retain change summaries only as descriptive.

Equal scheduled contact does not by itself ensure equal delivered dose or isolate a single mechanism. Record package components, fidelity, and actual minutes, and state that the estimand compares packages.

requests.purpose: Assess whether the supplied sample has enough students in provisional low-G1/high-absence strata to motivate a prospective trial and whether travel-time cross-strata are sparse. This is descriptive recruitment feasibility only; it cannot estimate an intervention effect.
requests.model_spec: No fitted model. Provisional screen G1<10; high absence absences>=6 (the supplied profile's 75th percentile); cross-tabulate traveltime categories 1-4. Report n and mean G2-G1 with a 95% t interval where n>=2. Do not select a threshold from outcome comparisons or call the result causal.
requests.code:
import json
import math
import pandas as pd
from scipy.stats import t

d = DF.loc[:, ['G1', 'G2', 'absences', 'traveltime']].copy()
d['eligible'] = d['G1'] < 10
d['high_absence'] = d['absences'] >= 6
d['change'] = d['G2'] - d['G1']
rows = []
for high in (False, True):
    for travel in (1, 2, 3, 4):
        g = d[(d['eligible']) & (d['high_absence'] == high) & (d['traveltime'] == travel)]
        n = int(len(g))
        mean = float(g['change'].mean()) if n else None
        if n >= 2:
            se = float(g['change'].std(ddof=1) / math.sqrt(n))
            half = float(t.ppf(0.975, n - 1) * se)
            ci = [mean - half, mean + half]
        else:
            ci = None
        rows.append({'high_absence': high, 'traveltime_category': travel, 'n': n, 'mean_G2_minus_G1': mean, 'ci95_t': ci})
print(json.dumps({'provisional_rules': {'G1_lt': 10, 'absences_gte': 6}, 'eligible_n': int(d['eligible'].sum()), 'strata': rows}, separators=(',', ':'), allow_nan=False))
